key_insight: VibeTraining-Bench evaluates whether research agents can improve AI systems by jointly refining training data, trainers, and inference harnesses.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark tests coordinated training and inference optimization under fixed resource budgets across mathematical reasoning, software engineering, terminal operation, and tool use.
method: Start each research agent from an identical target system and resource budget.
Use validation feedback to iteratively refine data, trainer, and inference harness, then submit a final system for test evaluation.
Isolate test data, separate research and grading containers, and restrict research-agent networking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that GPT-6-Astra improves SWE-bench Verified performance from 32.9% to 53.7%, compared with 55.4% for a human-developed instruct model.
watch_item: The abstract provides no mathematical-reasoning-specific results and notes remaining gaps in cumulative gains from iterative cross-component co-design.
paper_title: VibeTraining-Bench: Data-Trainer-Harness Co-Design for Iterative System Improvement
